source: Live Excel MCP operations on a new synthetic workbook
vba: Illustrative code only; no macros executed and no security settings changed.
python: Genuine pre-existing repository screenshot; no fresh Python execution claimed.

factReview.anthropicFinding: The published xlsx skill uses openpyxl for editing and LibreOffice for formula calculation. No claim that file-based workflows cannot calculate at all.
factReview.pythonFinding: Requires supported Microsoft 365, Python enabled, and internet. Python code executes in Microsoft's cloud, not locally.
factReview.vbaFinding: VBA project editing needs manually enabled trust. Macro execution changes the application's AutomationSecurity setting, so the video must not promise all security settings are preserved.
factReview.executionBoundary: Live evidence covers Power Query, Data Model/DAX, native PivotTable/PivotChart, and recalculation. VBA and Python are supported features, not newly executed demonstrations.
factReview.cliTokenFinding: The repository reports a same-task, same-model benchmark of about 59K CLI tokens versus 163K MCP tokens. The video says CLI can use fewer tokens for coding agents; it does not promise a fixed reduction for every client, model, or workflow.
